audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was given to Neeko at 7/10 and Level 6 was given to Neeko at 7/10, both against the packet chart, the mirror, and the page's own why-text.
audit.why: whys[0] says Level 1 is 'genuinely even' and whys[4] says 'even your Pop Blossom window is hers'. The mirror set row 0 to Skill 5/10 and row 4 to Irelia 7/10 from her side. A 33.33% win rate does not support Neeko owning two stages outright.
audit.corrected: Row 0 -> Skill (7/10 -> 5/10), row 4 -> Irelia (7/10 -> 3/10), both as matched full/content pairs in one group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Her item spike is attributed to 'passive shred' in three places — whys[5], late and wants.foe[2] — and once to 'BotRK-shred'. Ionian Fervor does not shred anything.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: striking enemies with spells grants stacking bonus attack speed, and at maximum stacks she gains bonus damage on hit. That is an attack-speed and on-hit spike, not a resistance shred — and the difference matters, because it means armour actually does help while attack-speed-scaled on-hit is what kills you. The mirror made the identical correction from Irelia's side.
audit.corrected: whys[5], whys[6], late and wants.foe[2] now name max-stack Ionian Fervor and BotRK's percent-health on-hit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance is described as blunting Neeko's burst — 'W eats your Q+R burst', 'your single combo doesn't kill a Defiant Dance damage-reduction window', 'pop W through your Q+R burst'. Neeko deals magic damage; Defiant Dance reduces physical damage.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Against a full-AP Neeko rotation the charge reduces nothing. Telling the player their combo is being absorbed by W teaches them to wait for a window that never mattered, and hides the ability that actually beats them — Bladesurge resetting off minions.
audit.corrected: mid, whys[5] and wants.foe[2] rewritten around the dash-reset and attack speed instead of the charge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet is the focus of the whole page and its cooldown is never stated; dosFull[2].d calls it 'the fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: It is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. At rank 1 that is a real window, and it is the only window in which stepping up is safe.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bladesurge heals her on every cast and every reset, and the only mention of anti-heal is four words of boilerplate attached to the wrong pronoun.
audit.why: _missing flags needs-antiheal for this matchup. Riot's Q text: she dashes to strike her target, healing herself, and the cooldown refreshes on a Marked target or a kill. In a wave she is healing continuously, which is why chip poke never sticks.

edits.before: Her Trinity/BotRK spike plus W damage-reduction tanks your full Q+R rotation and her shred kills you before it's back up.
edits.after: Her Trinity/BotRK spike plus max-stack Ionian Fervor attack speed out-damages your full Q+R rotation long before it is back up.

edits.before: Full-build Irelia dashes through your root, blocks your burst with W, and out-DPSes your squishy body — concede the duel and play for the map.
edits.after: Full-build Irelia dashes through your root and out-DPSes your squishy body on stacked on-hit damage — concede the duel and play for the map.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you cannot all-in without ult and she can, so farm with Q waveclear and refuse to face-tank her stun. At 6 Pop Blossom is your one saving grace, but it's a channel she can interrupt with her E stun, so use it REACTIVELY — let her commit the dash, then slam to AoE-stun her off you, ideally setting it up under tower or behind a Shapesplitter (W) clone so she misreads where you are. Realistically this stays her lane: she dashes through your root and your single combo doesn't kill a Defiant Dance (W) damage-reduction window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you cannot all-in without ult and she can, so farm with Q waveclear and refuse to face-tank her stun. At 6 Pop Blossom is your one saving grace, but the wind-up is exposed to her stun, so use it REACTIVELY — let her commit the dash, then slam to AoE-stun her off you, ideally from a disguise so the preparation stays hidden and she misreads where you are. Realistically this stays her lane: Defiant Dance only cuts physical damage, so what beats you is Bladesurge resetting off your own minions.

edits.before: She out-trades and out-scales you 1v1 once Trinity Force and Blade of the Ruined King come online — her W eats your Q+R burst and her passive shred plus auto-resets melt your squishy body before your rotation comes back up. Stop trying to win the duel. Your value is the map: shove with Q and roam, use disguise/clone pressure to make picks elsewhere, and become a teamfight bomb that AoE-stuns her whole team rather than the solo target she farms. Convert any early lead into objectives before her item spikes make the lane unplayable.
edits.after: She out-trades and out-scales you 1v1 once Trinity Force and Blade of the Ruined King come online — max-stack Ionian Fervor and BotRK's percent-health on-hit melt you before your rotation returns, and Bladesurge heals her on every reset unless you hold Grievous Wounds. Stop trying to win the duel. Your value is the map: shove with Q and roam, use disguise pressure to make picks, and be the teamfight bomb that stuns her whole team rather than the solo target she farms. Convert early leads into objectives before her spikes land.

edits.after: Stack Ionian Fervor attack speed, reset Bladesurge off your minions, then melt you with BotRK on-hit

edits.after: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 — dodge it and the dive falls apart. Commit inside that window.

edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. First: Stormsurge into Sorcerer's Shoes; then Shadowflame and Zhonya's into dive. Add anti-heal into Bladesurge healing.

notes: Left in place but unverified, same call the mirror made: spikes[2].text, whys[4] and wants.foe[1] all assert that Flawless Duet's stun cancels Pop Blossom mid-channel. Riot's text says only that Neeko 'leaps into the air' after a short preparation and that the preparation is hidden while disguised — it never defines what a stun during the leap does. Any hard CC during the preparation clearly stops it; whether the ability can still be interrupted after the leap begins is not in the file, so I did not sharpen those lines in either direction. Separately, the ability is written as 'Flawless Duet (Stun)' across eleven full-layer strings — the parenthetical is an editor's note that shipped as part of the name and wants a find/replace.
